thread_text:
oncall-bot: ALERT fired: high-p95 latency on /v1/generate for hosted-prod (region: us-west). Alert ID: A-2026-389. Severity: P2.
oncall-bot: Paging schedule: alex (primary), tanya (secondary).

alex: grabbing this handoff. quick summary: p95 spike started ~20m ago, error rate stable, requests queueing on transformer-infer-3.

tanya: noted. any customer-facing impact yet?

alex: limited so far — throughput throttled for some bursty clients; 504s for requests > 6k tokens if they hit the hot path. No broad outage. I've put rate-limit bypass off and added a temporary throttle at the edge for long requests.

matthew: putting this in context: last week we saw similar pattern after kernel upgrade, but there it was memory fragmentation. check /metrics/worker/transformer-infer-3/mem-alloc.

alex: running top-level checks:
```
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=transformer-infer-3
kubectl -n prod logs transformer-infer-3-abcde --since=15m | grep -i evict
curl -s https://observability.internal/alerts/A-2026-389
```

jessica: FYI I already kicked a canary fallback to model-variant v2-quant on a subset of routes (5% traffic) — latency improved for the canary.

alex: good call. mitigation plan I'm executing now:
- keep canary at 5% and observe for 10m
- if stable, increase to 25% by updating route weights (console: /routes/generate)
- run memory compaction on transformer nodes (see runbook).

tanya: coverage check: I'll be primary in 30m when alex goes to breakfast; can you leave clear steps? Also any runbook links?

alex: leaving notes now. Primary/secondary rotation: alex -> tanya at 1715003034. If escalates to P1, page SRE lead (@matthew) and exec-channel.

alex: runbook snippets: "If high-p95 with stable 5xx rate: 1) check worker mem and eviction logs; 2) enable model-variant fallback; 3) scale pool transformer-infer-3 by +2 pods; 4) request kernel page cache purge if OOM hints." Full runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-hotpath

oncall-bot: Note: Runbook link visited 3 times in last 10m.

tanya: thanks. covering notes: if fallbacks improve latency but error rate creeps up, we should revert and open a rollback to prior model version. Also watch cost — quant variant increases token cost by ~4%.

alex: mitigation in progress timeline:
- 1715001300: canary to v2-quant 5% (done)
- 1715001600: observed p95 drop from 820ms -> 240ms on canary
- 1715002000: will trigger mem compaction on node infer-3-a
- 1715002600: decision point to increase traffic to 25%

matthew: if mem compaction doesn't help within 10m, prepare to scale transformer-infer-3 pool (kubectl scale --replicas=+2). Also check NVMe io wait on nodes.

jessica: I've opened a short-lived customer advisory draft in #support-drafts describing limited latency impact for a subset of long-running generation requests. Will post after we decide on overall rollback or widen fallback.

alex: leaving this in tanya's hands at 1715003034. Key handoff pointers (short):
- Active alert A-2026-389 on /v1/generate p95 spike.
- Current mitigations: 5% v2-quant canary, edge throttle for >6k token requests.
- Next steps: mem compaction -> observe -> scale if needed -> widen canary to 25% if stable.
- Escalation: page SRE lead (@matthew) + execs for P1.
- Runbooks: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-hotpath and https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-evict
- Coverage gap: alex offdesk 1715003034-1715006634; tanya primary then.

tanya: acknowledged. I'll keep the thread updated every 10m or on any change. Leaving a quick checklist in here once I action something.

oncall-bot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance window between 1715010000-1715013600 — avoid non-essential restarts during that window.

alex: one more note — customer "BrightArc" has 8% of traffic on long requests. If we widen fallback, flag them in support draft.

tanya: got it. starting checks now: verifying node io and mem, will report back at 1715003634 or earlier if escalated.

matthew: standing by. if you need a fast scale I can approve immediate hot add to the pool.

jessica: will hold advisory until we decide to widen fallback.

alex: thanks everyone — leaving the channel in good shape. :thumbsup:

tanya: taking over now. updating thread as actions complete.
